root_causes.description: recommendation exhibits a saturated p99 latency pinned at the 10000 ms ceiling for the entire window, with a single trace p95_duration of ~5672504 ms, which cascades into frontend (its caller) also pinning at 10000 ms. Peer services (cart, ad) remain in the single-digit-to-low-ms range, isolating the anomaly to the recommendation path.

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000.0 ms (histogram ceiling), flat across the whole window
evidence.expected_baseline: p99 < 100 ms; peers in same window: cart p99 max=4.640 ms, ad p99 max=9.800 ms

root_causes.description: product-catalog is the shared downstream of both latency-affected services (frontend and recommendation) and shows an elevated CPU footprint (mean 2.754 cores, ~115x checkout's 0.024), consistent with a latency/saturation fault at the leaf propagating upward. No errors or restarts were observed on it, so a pure latency injection is the leading interpretation here.

frontend p99 is also pinned at the 10000 ms ceiling, but frontend is the entry aggregator that depends on recommendation and product-catalog, so its latency is most plausibly inherited from a downstream fault rather than self-inflicted.

evidence.observed_value: p99=10000.0 ms (histogram ceiling), flat across the whole window

remediation_steps: Confirm the latency fault on recommendation (or its shared downstream product-catalog): inspect per-call span durations via search_traces to find which handler is sleeping and check for a chaos/flagd fault toggle.
If a latency fault was injected, disable/roll back the fault and verify recommendation and frontend p99 return to baseline (<100 ms).
Check cgroup CPU throttling on product-catalog (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_seconds_total) and, if it is the source, raise its CPU limit and/or scale replicas.

Add/verify per-call deadlines, timeouts, and circuit breakers on frontend→recommendation and recommendation→product-catalog so a single slow dependency cannot cascade a 10 s p99 ceiling to the entry service.
Re-sweep error_rate, cpu_usage, memory_usage and pod_restarts across all main services to fully rule out concurrent faults on checkout, cart, payment, shipping, currency and ad.
